plan.topic: Tirzepatide hair shedding that seems to start months in: why it can show up after weight loss is under way
plan.angle:
08:00 calm 'Is this normal?' body moment.
- Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer) names tirzepatide and carries the relief fact: shedding linked to weight loss (telogen effluvium) typically shows up a couple of months after the trigger, according to AAD/DermNet timing used as typical ranges.
- Label stat: 5.4% vs 0.9% on placebo, Zepbound weight trials, population on the card. Don't claim the drug is the direct cause beyond the label's link to faster weight loss.
- Untagged lines: enough protein unless your clinician limits it; see a doctor if it's patchy, painful or lasts more than about 6 months.
- Close with the fixed don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and a loop line. 160 words or fewer.
- Post note (Exp G): target is Hair Loss.

package.title: Tirzepatide Hair Shedding Months In: Typical Timeline? #shorts
package.description:
Weight-loss shedding typically starts 2–4 months after the trigger. One likely explanation is telogen effluvium: resting hairs fall months later, so shedding lags behind weight loss. In Zepbound's weight trials in adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes, about 4–5 in 100 on tirzepatide reported hair loss vs about 1 in 100 on placebo. See a doctor if it's patchy, painful or lasts beyond about 6 months.
#Tirzepatide
Don't stop or change your medicine on your own.
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

script.cta: Spoken close, in the guide's order (no subscribe line, no 'link in the description'): "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber. Don't stop or change your medicine on your own." Then the loop line: "When you spot those strands, remember the timeline." Closing cards: two fixed, pre-split cards, 'NOT PERSONAL ADVICE, SO ASK YOUR PRESCRIBER.' then 'DON'T STOP OR CHANGE YOUR MEDICINE ON YOUR OWN.' POST NOTES: the Exp G watch-next target is Hair Loss (the publisher adds the verified related-video link). Word count: 159 spoken words by my own scene-by-scene count (s1 12, s2 17, s3 20, s4 19, s5 36, s6 31, s7 16, s8 8). 'weight-loss', "Zepbound's" and "Don't" each count as one word, so it's 160 if 'weight-loss' counts as two. That's inside the standard arm (135–160), about 68–72 s. Fact-check fixes applied: s3 card now reads 'One likely explanation: telogen effluvium'. s5 narration and stat_label add 'with or without type 2 diabetes' exactly as given, spoken as 'type two'. s4 second sentence is now 'Here is how common.' s8 is now 'When you spot those strands, remember the timeline.' The added clause is 6 words, not 5, so the fact-checker's total would have been 161. I cut 2 more words: s4 'stay put for a few months' became 'stay put a few months', and s3 'switch into' became 'enter'. Neither changes meaning or hedge. I didn't take the optional s1 rewrite: it would add a word, take the card past 6 words, and move the relief fact out of sentence 1. Sources are updated to the verified list.

factcheck.summary: I checked every factual claim against its primary source and they all hold. On the current DailyMed Zepbound label (Revised 11/2026), section 6.1 lists alopecia at 5% (5 mg), 4% (10 mg) and 5% (15 mg) versus 1% on placebo. Those figures come from a pool of Study 1 (no type 2 diabetes) and Study 2 (type 2 diabetes only), and the label links hair loss to weight reduction. DermNet (updated November 2019) gives the 2–4 month onset after a trigger, lists weight loss as a trigger and says acute cases taper over 6–9 months. AAD lists losing 20 pounds or more as a trigger, says shedding is noticed a few months later and says hair regains its fullness within 6–9 months. The hedges are kept ('one likely explanation', 'usually'), the comparator is named, the closing safety lines are fixed and in order, no individual dosing advice is given and the protein tip carries its caveat. My own count is also 158 words, inside the standard arm. What's left is minor polish: the s3 card is slightly stronger than its narration, the s5 population could be stated more precisely, and the hook wording is a little awkward. The pi.lilly.com PDF loads (985 KB) but couldn't be read as text. Its content and date are confirmed through the DailyMed listing of the same label.
